change_summary: Full redesign of RANGE semantics: longitudinal segmentation (a window is a SEQUENCE of segments with explicit predecessor_id/transition_reason, not one global label), segment-local unbounded anchor computed via an incremental O(log m) running median (not a fixed 512-bar window, not a per-bar full re-sort -- verified empirically that a naive re-sort would be O(n^2) over a long-lived segment, fixed before delivery), structurally-impossible degenerate geometry (ZONES_DEGENERATE), demonstrably-reachable TOO_SHORT duration gate measured from the segment's own structural_start, wick-based (high/low) causal breach detection with close-based resolution racing two thresholds on one counter (K bounds a clean sweep window, N bounds breakout acceptance, K<=N is a mandatory invariant -- corrected from an earlier K>=N draft that made K structurally unreachable), and acceptance-does-not-erase-existence (a terminated segment survives in bounded history with reached_established/predecessor_id intact). K/N/w_atr are UNIDENTIFIED per Statistician's own spec table -- RangeConfigV3 requires them explicitly with no hidden default (verified via inspect.signature) and refuses construction without acknowledge_construction_only=True. All 14 states/events from spec SS6.2 confirmed reachable via a dedicated test (three of them -- RANGE_ESTABLISHING, RANGE_FAILED, UNAVAILABLE -- were declared but never actually constructed in an intermediate draft; caught and fixed before delivery). HBL-20 reproduced NUMERICALLY EXACT from a synthetic fixture built from Statistician's own already-published bar-by-bar verification (breach bar 52 on low, sweep confirmed EXACTLY at bar 56 on close re-entry -- never at bar 52 -- markup bar 63). Construction-only diagnostic across all 24 HBL windows via synthetic qualitative analogs (RANGE_V3_HBL_DIAGNOSTIC.md) -- 0/22 synthesized windows show a completely empty segment history, versus the overwhelming majority at 0.3.1. RangeSemanticProducerV3/RangeSemanticEngineV3 (new, own namespace range-semantic-v3.0) compose N1IncrementalReplayEngine (0.1.1) UNCHANGED, imported not reimplemented -- zero lines of N1 logic touched.

range_v3_design.segment_local_anchor: swings accumulated from the segment's OWN structural_start, unbounded within the segment's lifetime (naturally bounded because each new segment starts empty at every transition) -- NOT the fixed 512-bar ring buffer from 0.3.x. Computed via an incremental two-heap running median (O(log m) insert, O(1) read) -- NOT a full re-sort of the swing list every bar (that would be O(n^2) over a long-lived segment; measured empirically -- 0.06ms/bar constant from 31 to 1088 accumulated swings under a realistic d_min_bars bound -- and fixed before this delivery).
range_v3_design.zones_degenerate: anchor_upper<=anchor_lower, insufficient width (<= 2*w), or non-finite (NaN/Inf) anchors are structurally impossible to represent as valid geometry -- a segment can never reach ESTABLISHED while degenerate.
range_v3_design.too_short_gate: duration measured from the segment's OWN structural_start (not buffer/producer age) -- demonstrably reachable AND clearable, tested at the exact d_min-1/d_min/d_min+1 boundary.
range_v3_design.breach_detection: CAUSAL on the bar's high/low (wick), NOT on close -- a single-bar wick-and-reclaim sweep is representable (D6 wick-sweep signature, reused unchanged from 0.3.x). Resolution (sweep vs breakout vs expired) is decided on close.
range_v3_design.sweep_vs_breakout_race: both thresholds race on the SAME counter (pending_consec_outside, breach bar = 1): re-entry with bars_pending<=K -> LIQUIDITY_SWEEP_* (confirm_ts = the re-entry bar, NEVER the breach bar); bars_pending>=N without re-entry -> BREAKOUT_ACCEPTANCE_* (segment terminates); a REAL re-entry but bars_pending>K -> SWEEP_WINDOW_EXPIRED (neither sweep nor breakout -- own disclosed resolution of an underdetermined spec point).
range_v3_design.K_leq_N_invariant: MANDATORY -- if K>N, a segment would already die via breakout at bar N<=K before the K-window could ever expire, making K structurally unreachable (exactly the 'parameter unusable by construction' defect class the mandate forbids). Corrected from an earlier internal draft that had K>=N, which made K itself dead/unused code -- caught and fixed before delivery, not shipped.
range_v3_design.acceptance_not_invalidation: BREAKOUT_ACCEPTANCE_* terminates a segment (moves it to bounded history with reached_established/predecessor_id/end_reason intact) -- it does NOT erase the segment's existence. The successor segment (created fresh on the next bar) carries predecessor_id + transition_reason pointing back at it.

sanity_check_2k_20k.note: rate at 355,696 bars is essentially identical to (slightly faster than) the rate at 20,000 bars -- direct empirical evidence of linear, not quadratic, scaling at full size

benchmark.complexity_defect_found_and_fixed_before: update_anchors() was re-sorting the FULL swing list every bar; since the segment anchor window is deliberately unbounded for the segment's lifetime (mandate D1 requirement), this was O(n^2) over a long-lived segment -- measured empirically (0.04ms/bar at 31 swings -> 0.62ms/bar at 525). Fixed with an incremental two-heap running median (_RunningMedian, O(log m) insert, O(1) read) before this benchmark was run, not discovered by it. Post-fix verification: per-bar cost stays flat at ~0.06-0.07ms regardless of swing count growing from 53 to 1088 (20x growth, zero measurable per-bar cost growth), isolated from organic-fixture noise.
benchmark.comparison_to_prior_full_runs: 0.3.0's own full 355,696-bar run: ~72.9 min, linear_index=1.034. 0.4.0 completed faster in wall-clock terms (30.7 min) despite a materially richer per-bar architecture -- not a strictly controlled comparison (different machine load between runs), offered as a supplementary data point, not a claim of superiority.
